propositions: Path.rglob on Python 3.11 caches directory entries and raises FileNotFoundError when a cached child directory disappears before descent, while Python 3.12 tolerates the same interleaving via walk-based enumeration

The snapshot teardown fixture recursively scans tmp_path and enters unrelated mutable subtrees including the live tracker lock directory, which is intentionally created and removed by the canonical store write lifecycle
A deterministic barrier demonstrates that real LockHandle.release() at a post-parent-scandir point reproduces the exact FileNotFoundError in the actual fixture on Python 3.11 but not 3.12

The repair replaces Path.rglob with os.walk(..., onerror=...) to ignore only FileNotFoundError for concurrently vanished entries while re-raising all other walk errors, retaining arbitrary-depth exact-root discovery

A held-out oracle test at tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py creates a real lock and snapshot tree, releases the lock at a deterministic barrier, and verifies cleanup removes the snapshot root while preserving adjacent content

A second monkeypatch-interaction defect exposed during mutation testing revealed that ambient Path(dirpath) factory calls in the cleanup path raise NotImplementedError on Python 3.11 when os.name is monkeypatched to 'nt', requiring scoped concrete-path selection
